title: Can You Eat A Tapeworm To Lose Weight?
summary: Josh and Chuck open with a plug for their upcoming book, then examine tapeworms: their anatomy (scolex with hooks and suckers, neck, proglottids), how they absorb nutrients without a mouth, life cycle through pigs, cows and humans, cysticercosis and its risks (including neurocysticercosis and seizures), prevention through hygiene and cooking meat to safe temperatures, and symptoms. They then cover the idea of swallowing a tapeworm to lose weight, the Victorian-era tapeworm diet pill ads, the Maria Callas urban legend, the alleged Tijuana "worm therapy" clinic, and why the idea is unhealthy. The episode ends with a listener mail from a high school student named Kate and a sign-off.
topics: eating a tapeworm to lose weight

segments.title: Book announcement and tapeworm teaser
segments.summary: Hosts plug their upcoming book Stuff You Should Know: An Incomplete Compendium of Mostly Interesting Things, then introduce the episode on tapeworms and the idea of eating one to lose weight.

segments.title: What tapeworms are and how they get them
segments.summary: Tapeworms are long parasites that can live in a host for decades. Infection usually comes from fecal contamination via poor hygiene or from undercooked meat, more commonly in developing countries and rural livestock areas. Hand washing is the key prevention.

segments.title: Tapeworm anatomy and nutrient absorption
segments.summary: A tapeworm has no mouth. Its scolex has suckers and hooks that anchor it to the intestinal wall. It absorbs nutrients through its skin, and some species, like the fish tapeworm, can cause vitamin B12 deficiency. The body is made of proglottids, with male segments near the head and female egg-holding segments farther down.

segments.title: Tapeworm life cycle and proglottid discharge
segments.summary: Proglottids break off and pass in stool, can crawl out of the anus, and may contaminate pasture. Cows ingest eggs, larvae form cysts in muscle, and humans who eat undercooked meat get the adult worm, completing the cycle. Dogs scooting is mentioned as a possible sign.

segments.title: Cysticercosis and health dangers
segments.summary: Ingesting tapeworm eggs can cause cysticercosis, where larvae enter the bloodstream and lodge in tissues. Effects include blindness if near the eye, brain damage, and adult-onset seizures; a neurocysticercosis estimate is cited. Large worms can block ducts or rupture, causing severe allergic reaction.

segments.title: Prevention, cooking temperatures, and resting steak
segments.summary: The US meat industry screens for tapeworm cysts, but the government recommends minimum cooking temperatures. Letting cooked meat rest for at least three minutes kills parasites, and the hosts debate resting technique and steak cooking methods.

segments.title: Symptoms and diagnosis of tapeworm
segments.summary: Symptoms can include weakness, diarrhea, dizziness, appetite loss, weight loss, salt cravings, and pica. Diagnosis involves a stool sample, and treatment uses an antiparasitic drug that paralyzes the worm so it passes out. The same drug is studied for other conditions.

segments.title: Break before final act
segments.summary: Short break before the weight-loss section.

segments.title: Tapeworm as a weight-loss aid: history and myths
segments.summary: Hosts explain that swallowing a tapeworm to lose weight is a bad idea. Victorian-era tapeworm pill ads targeted women, and Maria Callas's weight loss is linked to a tapeworm in an urban legend. A Tijuana clinic called Worm Therapy is rumored to offer tapeworm treatment, but this is unverified. Tapeworms steal nutrients and can cause malnutrition and rebound weight gain.
